ai.title: Fix file creation by handling optional file reads
ai.summary: Added `requestOptionalFile` and `toOptionalFile` to safely handle file reads that may return null or error statuses, replacing direct `requestFile` usage in `main-prompt.ts`. Updated `project-files.ts` with `getFilesOrNull` to filter out hidden file read statuses before processing changes. Fixed a variable scope error in `changes.ts` where `path` was incorrectly used instead of `filePath` in error logging.

eli5.text: When the assistant tried to create a new file in a project, it could sometimes fail if it attempted to read an existing file that didn’t exist or had restricted access. Now, the system gracefully handles those missing or inaccessible file reads instead of crashing, so file creation succeeds more reliably. If you tried to add a file and it unexpectedly errored before, it should now complete without that issue.

ai.title: parseToolCallXml returns strings only
ai.summary: parseToolCallXml in backend/src/util/parse-tool-call-xml.ts now returns Record<string, string>, removing type coercion for booleans, numbers, and nested range tags. All XML values are assigned as raw strings after whitespace trimming. Scope limited to backend utility; no CLI or Web surface changes indicated. This simplifies parsing logic by delegating type interpretation to consumers.

eli5.text: The program that reads tool-call instructions now keeps every value from the XML as plain text, for example, a 5000 timeout stays "5000" and a true flag becomes "true" instead of being converted to the number 5000 or the on/off value true. This only affects the backend utility that parses those instructions, so no changes appear in the assistant itself today; if you were to inspect the parsed data, all entries would now be strings rather than a mix of strings, numbers, and boolean values.

ai.title: Switch Relace AI fallback from Gemini Flash to o3-mini
ai.summary: Relace API fallback logic in backend/src/llm-apis/relace-api.ts now invokes promptOpenAI with models.o3mini instead of promptGeminiWithFallbacks with geminiModels.gemini2flash. The prompt instruction changed to allow markdown output, with results processed via parseMarkdownCodeBlock to extract code. This replaces the previous direct text return mechanism.

eli5.text: When the assistant's main service for rewriting files has a problem, it now asks a different helper for help instead of the one it used before. If you use the file-rewriting feature, you won't see a change in how it works, but the system behind it is relying on a different source when it needs a backup.

ai.title: Refactor checkpoint error handling and imports
ai.summary: CheckpointManager.disabledReason now stores a string instead of a CheckpointsDisabledError instance, requiring explicit error construction on throw. CLI and client.ts updated to read the string directly, and getLatestCheckpoint wrapped in try/catch to handle disabled states gracefully. Import statements across checkpoint-manager.ts, cli.ts, and client.ts reordered for consistency.

eli5.text: When the checkpointing system is turned off, it now records the reason as plain text instead of saving a structured error object. When you check status or interact with checkpoints, the system will read that plain reason directly and handle the disabled state without throwing a broken error. Internally, the code that wires these pieces together was reorganized for consistency, but your experience stays the same: if checkpoints are disabled, you'll still see a clear message instead of a crash.

ai.title: Refactor simplify-tool-results, add terminal command simplifier
ai.summary: Extracted generic `simplifyToolResults` helper into new `backend/src/util/simplify-tool-results.ts`. Added `simplifyTerminalCommandResults` for `run_terminal_command` outputs. Moved `simplifyReadFileResults` out of `parse-tool-call-xml.ts`. Removes `read_files` specific logic from XML parser.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the assistant's internal tool-processing system was cleaned up and made more flexible. Previously, the code that simplified file-reading results was tangled up inside the main tool parser, making it hard to reuse for other tools. Now, a single, more general-purpose helper was extracted into its own module, and a new specialized version was added to also clean up and simplify the verbose output from terminal/shell command executions. While you won't directly see a new feature, the assistant's backend is now more organized, easier to maintain, and prepared to consistently tidy up a wider variety of tool outputs it generates, including those from terminal commands. This is a live internal refactor available today.

eli5.text: The assistant's version number was updated to 1.0.198 as part of a routine update. This is a behind-the-scenes change that only affects how the software is packaged and distributed. The update also includes several small improvements to how files are handled and how the assistant interacts with different AI services. You wouldn't notice any major differences in how the assistant works.

ai.title: yes command blacklist updated to multi-word check
ai.summary: Refactored `isBlacklistedTerminalCommand` in `backend/src/check-terminal-command.ts` to distinguish single-word from multi-word commands. `yes` moved from `blacklistedSingleWordCommands` to `blacklistedMultiWordCommands`. Logic now checks the first word for multi-word entries. Prevents false positives for commands like `yesterday` while blocking `yes`.

ai.title: Fix import paths in main-prompt.ts
ai.summary: Corrects import statements in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Functions `simplifyReadFileResults` and `simplifyReadFileToolResult` are now imported from `./util/simplify-tool-results` instead of `./util/parse-tool-call-xml`. This aligns imports with actual module structure.

eli5.text: The system adjusted where a couple of internal helper tools are loaded from, so they now come from the toolbox they're actually kept in instead of an old, mismatched shelf. This only touches internal wiring, so you as a regular user won't notice anything different in how the assistant responds or operates today.

ai.title: Logger context adds logTrace field with user info
ai.summary: Logger mixin now wraps AsyncLocalStorage context in a `logTrace` field instead of spreading it directly. Middleware resolves `UserInfo` via `getUserInfoFromAuthToken` and injects `userId`, `userEmail`, `discordId`, and `clientSessionId` into the logger context. Affects `backend/src/util/logger.ts`, `backend/src/websockets/auth.ts`, and `backend/src/websockets/middleware.ts`. Removed `silent` flag from middleware halt logging.

eli5.text: When you send a message to the backend, each log entry now carries a labeled package called a logTrace that includes your user info like email and Discord name along with your session ID. Instead of scattering your details all over the log, the system tucks them neatly into this one place for every request you make. The logs also got quieter when things are intentionally paused, so there's less noise if a request is held back. This is live today for anyone using the service behind the scenes.
